transcription.tex: \textbf{Mechanics Year 1 · Chapter 10}\par \textbf{Forces and Motion}\par Force diagrams and equilibrium\par Newton’s laws\par Connected particles and pulleys
Use \(g=9.8\text{ m/s}^2\) unless otherwise stated. Choose a positive direction and draw the forces on each body separately.

transcription.tex: 1. Calculate \((2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)+(3\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)\) and \((-\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)-(3\mathbf i-\mathbf j)\).\par 2. A right triangle has perpendicular sides 12 cm and 15 cm. Find its hypotenuse and the angle opposite the 12 cm side to 1 d.p.\par 3. A car accelerates from rest at \(1.5\text{ m/s}^2\) for 12 s. Find its speed. It then decelerates at \(1\text{ m/s}^2\): find its stopping distance.
1. \(5\mathbf i-3\mathbf j\); \(-4\mathbf i+4\mathbf j\).

transcription.tex: \textbf{Force diagrams}\par Weight \(W=mg\) acts vertically downwards. Normal reaction \(R\) is perpendicular to the contact surface. Tension acts along a taut string, away from the body. Friction opposes relative sliding or its tendency.\par \textbf{Newton’s first law}\par Zero resultant force means constant velocity (including rest).\par An object has forces 30 N right, 30 N left, 40 N up and 5 N down. Find the resultant.
\[F_x=30-30=0,\qquad F_y=40-5=35.\] The resultant is 35 N upwards. Acceleration is in the direction of the resultant force.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: 1. Forces act on a particle: \(P\) N right, 3 N left, 5 N up and 5 N down. Find the resultant.\par 2. Forces act on another particle: 5 N right, 7 N left, 4 N up and 6 N down. Find the resultant and its magnitude.
1. \(\mathbf F=(P-3)\mathbf i\) N. Its direction depends on whether \(P\) is greater or less than 3.
2. \(\mathbf F=-2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j\) N.\[|\mathbf F|=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt2\text{ N}.\] It points diagonally down and left.

transcription.tex: 1. Forces \((2,3),(4,-1),(-3,2),(a,b)\) N are in equilibrium. Find \(a,b\).\par 2. With \(\mathbf i\) east and \(\mathbf j\) north, find the resultant, magnitude and bearing of forces \((2,1),(3,-2),(-1,4)\) N.
2. \(\mathbf R=4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j\) N.\[|\mathbf R|=5\text{ N}.\]\[\theta=\tan^{-1}(4/3)=053.1^\circ.\]

transcription.tex: 1. Forces \((7\mathbf i-9\mathbf j),(5\mathbf i+6\mathbf j),(p\mathbf i+q\mathbf j)\) N are in equilibrium. Find \(p,q\). Remove the third force: find the resultant’s magnitude and angle with \(\mathbf j\), to the nearest degree.\par 2. Forces \((\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)\) N and \((p\mathbf i+2p\mathbf j)\) N act on a particle. Find the first force’s angle with \(\mathbf j\), and \(p>0\) if the resultant is parallel to \(\mathbf i\).
1. \(p=-12,q=3\).\[\mathbf R=12\mathbf i-3\mathbf j.\]\[|\mathbf R|=3\sqrt{17}=12.4\text{ N}.\] Angle with \(\mathbf j\): \(90^\circ+\tan^{-1}(3/12)=104^\circ\).
2. Angle \(=180^\circ-\tan^{-1}(1/3)=161.6^\circ\).\[-3+2p=0\Rightarrow p=\tfrac32.\]

transcription.tex: \textbf{Extension}\par A force \(F_1\) acts in the direction of \(\mathbf i\); a force \(F_2\) acts at angle \(\theta\) to \(\mathbf i\). Show that the resultant has magnitude\[\sqrt{F_1^2+F_2^2+2F_1F_2\cos\theta}.\]
\[\mathbf R=(F_1+F_2\cos\theta)\mathbf i+F_2\sin\theta\mathbf j\] \[|\mathbf R|^2=(F_1+F_2\cos\theta)^2+F_2^2\sin^2\theta\]
\[=F_1^2+2F_1F_2\cos\theta+F_2^2(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)\] \[=F_1^2+F_2^2+2F_1F_2\cos\theta.\] Take the non-negative square root.

transcription.tex: \textbf{Newton’s second law}\[\mathbf F_{\rm resultant}=m\mathbf a\]\par 1. A 2000 kg car has driving force 800 N and resistance 200 N. Find its acceleration.\par 2. Find the weight of a 50 kg child.\par 3. A falling 70 kg body experiences 300 N air resistance. Find its acceleration.
3. Downwards positive:\[70g-300=70a\Rightarrow a=5.51\text{ m/s}^2.\]

transcription.tex: A 5 kg body is pulled from rest along a rough horizontal table by a horizontal force of 20 N. Friction is 4 N. Find:\par a. its acceleration;\par b. its displacement in the first 4 s;\par c. the normal reaction.
a. \(20-4=5a\Rightarrow a=3.2\text{ m/s}^2\).
c. No vertical acceleration:\[R-5g=0\Rightarrow R=49\text{ N}.\]

transcription.tex: A particle of mass 4 kg reaches soft horizontal ground with downward speed 28 m/s. The ground exerts a constant upward resistive force of 5000 N. Find how far the particle sinks before coming to rest.
Downwards positive:\[4g-5000=4a\Rightarrow a=-1240.2\text{ m/s}^2.\]

transcription.tex: 9. A lift of mass 500 kg carries passengers of total mass 300 kg. It accelerates from rest to 3 m/s over 5 m. Find:\par a. the acceleration magnitude;\par b. cable tension when accelerating downwards;\par c. cable tension when accelerating upwards.
a. \(3^2=2a(5)\Rightarrow a=0.9\text{ m/s}^2\).

transcription.tex: 10. A 50 kg trolley is pulled from rest along a horizontal path by a horizontal rope. After 2 s its speed is 1 m/s. Constant resistance is 20 N. Find:\par a. its acceleration;\par b. rope tension.
b. \(T-20=50(0.5)\Rightarrow T=45\) N.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: 11. A 400 kg van moves at 16 m/s when its engine cuts out. It stops without braking. Model the resistance as a constant 200 N. Find:\par a. the stopping time;\par b. stopping distance;\par c. a limitation of this model.
a. \(-200=400a\Rightarrow a=-0.5\text{ m/s}^2\).\[0=16-0.5t\Rightarrow t=32\text{ s}.\]
c. Air resistance usually depends on speed, so constant resistance is an approximation.

transcription.tex: \textbf{Motion in two dimensions}\par Force, acceleration, velocity and displacement are vectors. Mass, area and volume are scalars.\par A resultant force \((3\mathbf i+8\mathbf j)\) N acts on a 0.5 kg particle. Take \(\mathbf i\) east and \(\mathbf j\) north. Find its acceleration vector, magnitude and bearing.
\[\mathbf a=\frac{\mathbf F}{m}=6\mathbf i+16\mathbf j\text{ m/s}^2.\]

transcription.tex: A 60 kg boat experiences forces \((80,50)\), \((10p,20q)\) and \((-75,100)\) N. Its acceleration is \((0.8,-1.5)\text{ m/s}^2\). Find \(p,q\).
\[5+10p=48\Rightarrow p=4.3\] \[150+20q=-90\Rightarrow q=-12.\]

transcription.tex: 3. A particle of mass 3 kg has acceleration \((7\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)\text{ m/s}^2\). Find its resultant force, magnitude and bearing. Take \(\mathbf i\) east and \(\mathbf j\) north.
\[\mathbf F=3(7\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)=21\mathbf i-9\mathbf j\text{ N}.\]
\[|\mathbf F|=\sqrt{522}=22.8\text{ N}\] \[\text{Bearing}=90^\circ+\tan^{-1}(9/21)=113^\circ\] to the nearest degree.

Write \(\mathbf R=k(-\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)\). Comparing components:\[2+p=-k,\qquad3+q=4k.\]

transcription.tex: 7. A 4 kg particle starts from rest under constant force \((6\mathbf i+b\mathbf j)\) N, bearing \(045^\circ\). Find:\par a. \(b\);\par b. force magnitude;\par c. acceleration magnitude;\par d. distance travelled in 5 s.
a. Equal positive components: \(b=6\).\par b. \(|\mathbf R|=6\sqrt2\) N.
c. \(a=6\sqrt2/4=3\sqrt2/2\text{ m/s}^2\).

\textbf{Challenge}\par A 0.5 kg particle experiences forces \(-4\mathbf i\) N and \((k\mathbf i+2k\mathbf j)\) N. Its acceleration magnitude is \(8\sqrt{17}\) m/s². Find \(k>0\).

transcription.tex: Particles \(P,Q\), masses 5 kg and 3 kg, are joined by a light inextensible string on a rough horizontal plane. A horizontal 40 N force pulls \(P\) away from \(Q\). Friction is 10 N on \(P\) and 6 N on \(Q\).\par a. Find their acceleration.
For the whole system the internal tensions cancel:\[40-10-6=(5+3)a\Rightarrow a=3\text{ m/s}^2.\]
Alternatively, for the separate particles:\[40-T-10=5a,\qquad T-6=3a.\] Adding gives \(24=8a\), as before.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: Particles \(P,Q\), masses 5 kg and 3 kg, are joined by a light inextensible string on a rough horizontal plane. A horizontal 40 N force pulls \(P\) away from \(Q\). Friction is 10 N on \(P\) and 6 N on \(Q\).\par b. Find the tension.\par c. Explain the string assumptions.
b. For \(Q\): \(T-6=3(3)\Rightarrow T=15\) N.
c. Light: negligible mass and uniform tension.\par Inextensible and taut in this arrangement: both particles have the same acceleration.

transcription.tex: \textbf{Newton’s third law}\par Interaction forces on two different bodies are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.\par A light scale-pan carries \(A\) (0.4 kg) on top of \(B\) (0.6 kg). A light vertical string raises the pan with acceleration \(0.5\text{ m/s}^2\). Find:\par a. string tension;\par b. force on \(B\) by \(A\);\par c. force on \(B\) by the pan.
a. \(T-1g=1(0.5)\Rightarrow T=10.3\) N.
b. For \(A\): \(R-0.4g=0.4(0.5)\Rightarrow R=4.12\) N. Hence \(A\) exerts 4.12 N downwards on \(B\).
c. For both masses: \(N-1g=1(0.5)\Rightarrow N=10.3\) N upwards.

transcription.tex: A 50 kg woman stands in a 950 kg lift. It moves upwards with constant deceleration \(2\text{ m/s}^2\). Find:\par a. cable tension;\par b. the force on the woman by the floor.
a. Upwards positive, acceleration is \(-2\):\[T-1000g=1000(-2)\]\[T=7800\text{ N}.\]
b. \(R-50g=50(-2)\Rightarrow R=390\) N.

transcription.tex: 1. Particles \(P,Q\) of masses 8 kg and 2 kg are joined by a light inextensible taut string on a smooth horizontal plane. A force \(F\) pulls \(P\) away from \(Q\), giving acceleration \(0.4\text{ m/s}^2\). Find \(F\), tension and explain the assumptions.
Light gives uniform tension and negligible string mass. Inextensible and taut gives equal accelerations along this straight string.

transcription.tex: 5. A lorry of mass \(m\) kg tows a trailer of mass \(3m\) kg using a light inextensible tow-bar. Driving force is 50,000 N; resistances are 4,000 N on the lorry and 10,000 N on the trailer. Acceleration is \(5\text{ m/s}^2\). Find both masses and tow-bar tension; explain the assumptions.
The light bar has negligible mass; its end forces have equal magnitudes. Its fixed length gives equal accelerations.

For \(B\): \(T-5g=5(2.2)\Rightarrow T=60\) N.

\[T-4g=4(2)\Rightarrow T=47.2\text{ N}.\]

transcription.tex: 8. A 6400 kg engine pulls a 1600 kg carriage using a light horizontal coupling. Driving force is 12,000 N; resistances are \(R\) N on the engine and 2000 N on the carriage. Acceleration is \(0.5\text{ m/s}^2\). Find \(R\) and show the coupling tension is 2800 N.
For carriage:\[T-2000=1600(0.5)\Rightarrow T=2800\text{ N}.\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: 9. A 900 kg car pulls a 300 kg trailer through a light tow-bar. Resistances are 200 N and 100 N respectively; driving force is 1200 N.\par a. Show acceleration is \(0.75\text{ m/s}^2\).\par b. Find tension.\par c. The engine force becomes zero and brakes exert \(F\) N on the car. Resistances stay the same and the bar’s thrust is 100 N. Find \(F\).
c. Trailer deceleration: \(d=(100+100)/300=2/3\).\par For car, backwards positive:\[F+200-100=900(2/3)\Rightarrow F=500\text{ N}.\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: \textbf{Pulleys}\par Particles \(P,Q\), masses \(2m,3m\), hang from a light inextensible string over a small smooth fixed pulley. Release from rest with string taut.\par Find their acceleration, tension, force on the pulley by the string, and \(Q\)’s displacement after 4 s, assuming neither particle reaches an obstruction.
For \(P\) upwards and \(Q\) downwards:\[T-2mg=2ma,\quad3mg-T=3ma.\] \[a=g/5,\quad T=12mg/5.\]
Both string forces on the pulley act downwards:\[F=2T=24mg/5.\] \[s=\tfrac12(g/5)(4^2)=15.7\text{ m}.\]
A light string over a smooth pulley has equal tension on both sides. The taut inextensible string gives equal acceleration magnitudes in this fixed-pulley arrangement.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: Particles \(A\) (0.4 kg) and \(B\) (0.8 kg) are connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth fixed table-edge pulley. \(A\) is on a rough table, 4.5 m from the pulley; \(B\) hangs 0.5 m above ground. Friction on \(A\) is \(0.08g\) N. Released from rest, find acceleration, time until \(B\) lands, and total distance travelled by \(A\).
The string becomes slack. For \(A\), \(a=-0.08g/0.4=-1.96\).\[0=5.88-2(1.96)s\Rightarrow s=1.5\text{ m}.\] Total distance \(=0.5+1.5=2.0\) m.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: Particles \(A,B\), masses \(5m,km\) with \(k<5\), hang at equal heights from a light inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley. Released from rest, \(A\) descends at acceleration \(g/4\).\par a. Show \(T=15mg/4\).\par b. Find \(k\).\par c. Explain “smooth”.\par d. \(A\) hits ground after 1.2 s. Find \(B\)’s greatest height above ground, assuming it does not reach the pulley.
a. \(5mg-T=5m(g/4)\).\par \(T=15mg/4\).\par b. \(T-kmg=km(g/4)\Rightarrow k=3\).\par c. Equal tensions on either side of the pulley.

d. Initial height \(h=\tfrac12(g/4)(1.2^2)=0.18g\).\par When \(A\) lands, \(B\) has height \(2h\) and speed \(0.3g\). Additional rise:\[s=\frac{(0.3g)^2}{2g}=0.045g.\] Greatest height \(=0.405g=3.97\) m.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: 1. Masses 4 kg and 3 kg hang from a light inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley, released from rest.\par a. Find tension.\par b. The 4 kg mass falls 2 m before landing. Find its impact speed.\par c. Find the other mass’s greatest height above its initial position, assuming it does not reach the pulley.
\[4g-T=4a,\quad T-3g=3a\Rightarrow a=g/7.\] \[T=24g/7=33.6\text{ N}.\]
Additional free rise \(=v^2/(2g)=2/7\) m.\par Total rise \(=2+2/7=16/7\) m.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: 2. Masses \(km,3m\) hang initially at equal heights from a light inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley. On release the heavier mass descends at \(g/3\) and hits ground after 1.8 s.\par a. Find tension.\par b. Show \(k=1.5\).\par c. Explain “smooth”.\par d. Show the lighter mass reaches height \(1.26g\) m above ground without reaching the pulley.
\[3mg-T=3m(g/3)\Rightarrow T=2mg.\] \[T-kmg=km(g/3)\Rightarrow k=1.5.\] Smooth pulley gives equal tensions.
Initial height \(h=\tfrac12(g/3)(1.8^2)=0.54g\).\par Speed at landing \(v=0.6g\). Extra rise \(=v^2/(2g)=0.18g\).\[H=2(0.54g)+0.18g=1.26g\text{ m}.\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: 3. Masses \(A=m\) kg and \(B=3\) kg, with \(m>3\), hang from a light inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley. Released from rest, \(A\) descends 2.5 m in 1.25 s and stops on the ground.\par a. Show acceleration is \(3.2\text{ m/s}^2\).\par b. Find tension.\par c. Show \(m=65/11\).
a. \(2.5=\tfrac12a(1.25^2)\Rightarrow a=3.2\text{ m/s}^2\).
b. \(T-3g=3(3.2)\Rightarrow T=39\) N.
c. \(mg-T=ma\Rightarrow m=39/(9.8-3.2)=65/11\) kg.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: 3. Continued: \(A\) hits the ground after descending for 1.25 s with acceleration \(3.2\text{ m/s}^2\). The string becomes slack and \(B\) moves freely without reaching the pulley.\par d. Explain how inextensibility was used.\par e. Find the time from impact until the string becomes taut again.
d. While taut, the fixed string length makes the particles’ acceleration magnitudes equal. Equal tension instead follows from the light string and smooth pulley.
e. At impact, \(u_B=3.2(1.25)=4\) m/s. The string becomes taut when \(B\) returns to this height:\[0=4t-4.9t^2\Rightarrow t=\frac{40}{49}=0.816\text{ s}.\]

transcription.tex: 5. A 2.5 kg box on a rough table is connected to a hanging 1.5 kg sphere by a light inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley. Friction is \(k\) N. Released from rest, the sphere falls 0.8 m in 0.75 s.\par a. Find acceleration, tension and \(k\).\par b. Explain how inextensibility was used.
\[k=T-2.5a=3.3222\ldots=3.32\text{ N}.\] Retain unrounded values during the calculation.
While the string is taut, its fixed length gives equal acceleration magnitudes for the box and sphere.
